explanation: In uniform circular motion the speed v is constant but the velocity VECTOR continuously changes direction, so there is an acceleration. The velocity is always tangent to the circle (blue arrow); the acceleration points toward the center (pink arrow) and has magnitude a_c = v^2/r, with angular speed omega = v/r. Because nothing speeds the object up, there is no tangential acceleration — the net acceleration is purely radial (centripetal). On the AP exam, recognizing that 'constant speed' still means 'accelerating, directed inward' is the key conceptual hurdle this animation makes visible.
bullets: Velocity (blue) is always tangent to the circle.
Acceleration (pink) always points to the center.
Magnitude a_c = v^2/r; angular speed omega = v/r.
Constant speed, changing direction = nonzero acceleration.
